notice: Bibliographic grounding is not passage-level verification. See individual verification fields. No source text was copied into the examples.

thinkers.name: Krishna as presented in the Bhagavad Gita
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: A sacred dialogue with diverse Vedanta and other interpretations; Krishna is not reduced to a productivity coach.

thinkers.name: Aristotle
references: Nicomachean Ethics, books II, VI, VIII-IX
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Virtue is context-sensitive, not an arithmetic middle; his historical exclusions are not endorsed.

thinkers.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
references: On the Genealogy of Morality, essay I
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Interpretations of power and affirmation are contested; self-creation does not imply permission to abuse.

thinkers.name: Sigmund Freud
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Historically influential interpretations are not established diagnoses or substitutes for current evidence.

thinkers.name: Carl Jung
references: The Relations between the Ego and the Unconscious
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Symbolic readings are hypotheses, not universal codes or proof of supernatural events.

thinkers.name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Fiction stages conflicting voices; a character is not a transparent mouthpiece for the author.

thinkers.name: Robert Greene
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Popular strategic frameworks and historical anecdotes are not validated universal laws; ethical filters are editorial.

thinkers.name: Viktor Frankl
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Meaning is not a cure-all; constraints on agency and the need to change avoidable suffering matter.

thinkers.name: Arthur Schopenhauer
references: The World as Will and Representation, volume I, books III-IV
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Metaphysical pessimism is not a clinical conclusion or an argument for self-harm.

thinkers.name: Blaise Pascal
references: Pensees, fragments on diversion, the wager, and the orders
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Fragment numbering varies by edition; the wager is not a neutral proof that settles religious pluralism.

thinkers.name: Daniel Kahneman
references: Maps of Bounded Rationality: A Perspective on Intuitive Judgment and Choice, Nobel lecture (2002)
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Many insights were developed with Amos Tversky and others; a bias label alone does not prove an error.

thinkers.name: Oliver Sacks
references: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Narrative cases are not representative datasets; respect privacy and do not infer diagnoses from literary analogies.

thinkers.name: Thomas Hobbes
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Historical support for strong sovereignty is not a modern rights framework; acknowledge the tension.

thinkers.name: John Locke
references: Second Treatise of Government, chapters II, V, IX, XIX
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Historical exclusions and colonial entanglements limit claims that his framework was fully inclusive.

thinkers.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
references: Discourse on the Origin and Foundations of Inequality
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: General will is not identical to any majority vote; coercive and exclusionary implications require scrutiny.

thinkers.name: Karl Marx
references: Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, Estranged Labour
Capital, volume I, chapters on the labour process and working day
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Structural analysis does not establish that every conflict has one cause or justify political violence.

thinkers.name: Friedrich Hayek
references: The Use of Knowledge in Society (1945)
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Knowledge arguments do not establish that markets solve every externality, power imbalance, or equity problem.

thinkers.name: Alexis de Tocqueville
references: Democracy in America, volume I, part II; volume II, parts II and IV
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: His account has historical blind spots; participation does not automatically protect minorities.

thinkers.name: Albert Camus
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Absurdity is not a recommendation of despair; ethical revolt resists sacrificing people to abstractions.

thinkers.name: Jean-Paul Sartre
references: Being and Nothingness, discussion of bad faith
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Freedom is exercised within material and social constraints; do not equate oppression with a chosen attitude.

thinkers.name: Soren Kierkegaard
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Pseudonymous works explore distinct positions; faith is not a blanket warrant for overriding ethics.

thinkers.name: Epictetus
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: The distinction of agency is not an instruction to tolerate injustice or suppress emotion.

thinkers.name: Confucius
references: Analects, books II, XII, XIII, XV
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Role ethics has hierarchical dimensions; respectful criticism and contemporary equality must be distinguished.

thinkers.name: Early Buddhist teachings associated with the Buddha
references: Samyutta Nikaya 56.11, Discourse on Setting the Wheel of Dhamma in Motion
Majjhima Nikaya 58, discourse to Prince Abhaya
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Buddhist traditions differ; a modern advice exercise does not exhaust liberation, ethics, or meditation practice.

thinkers.name: Sun Tzu
references: The Art of War, chapters III and VI
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Ancient military advice is adapted selectively; workplace conflicts are not literal wars.

thinkers.name: Niccolo Machiavelli
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Acknowledge morally troubling arguments rather than presenting a fully humane historical doctrine.

thinkers.name: Mary Wollstonecraft
references: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, chapters II-IV and XII
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Her account has period-specific limits; contemporary inclusive applications are editorial extensions.

thinkers.name: W. E. B. Du Bois
references: The Souls of Black Folk, Of Our Spiritual Strivings
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Double consciousness has a specific Black American history and is not merely generic self-consciousness.

thinkers.name: Hannah Arendt
references: The Human Condition, chapters on action
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: The banality of evil is a contested analysis, not a claim that wrongdoing is harmless or all perpetrators identical.

thinkers.name: B. R. Ambedkar
thinkers.interpretation_caveat: Caste has institutional and inherited dimensions; it is not reducible to interpersonal prejudice.
